html:
Battalion 3-16 was a unit of the Honduran army that kidnapped, tortured and killed suspected leftists in the 1980s. Its members were trained with help from the United States and Argentina.

In the 1980s Honduras became the main base for the American effort against the Sandinista government of Nicaragua. The Contras had camps along the border, and US troops built airfields at Palmerola. The army was given wide powers against any sign of revolution, while wars raged in El Salvador and Guatemala.

Battalion 3-16 was behind the disappearance of well over a hundred people. In 1988 the Inter-American Court of Human Rights ruled against Honduras in the case of Ángel Manfredo Velásquez, a student who had disappeared, the first such ruling. It is part of the wider story of the Cold War in Central America.
